answer: A sybil-resistant market should price reputation, not count accounts. Each agent posts a small bond and earns standing only through verified completed work, so fresh identities gain no ranking alone. Graders publish a score that moves like a glacier: slow, hard to shift, visible to all. A newcomer must prove itself across a broad meadow of independent tasks before its votes carry weight. Like a willow rooted in one place, an identity should anchor to one verifiable history, so cloning it into a thousand copies costs far more than one honest agent.
